candidate: Eastern collared lizard (Crotaphytus collaris collaris), Peck Ranch experimental restoration/reintroduction metapopulation

scientific_anchor.published_design: translocation/reintroduction beginning in 1984 on restored Ozark glades followed by long-term glade-level monitoring
scientific_anchor.source_process_claim: known managed introductions are external additions and are represented prospectively by glade and year; natural expansion among the mapped glade/section universe is the target process. Any additional unmanaged external source not representable before response access stops the candidate.
scientific_anchor.historical_anchor: 1980 extensive Peck Ranch survey reported no collared-lizard populations; prescribed woodland burning began in 1994 and initiated the high-colonization phase; a stable metapopulation phase was established by about 2000.

managed_source_schedule.semantic_unit: source activation at founder glade in release year; founder count is deliberately not used because published descriptions differ on the first release count
managed_source_schedule.evidence_boundary: glade/year identities are concordant across the 2001 PNAS study, 2013 Molecular Ecology study and later restoration summaries; no response table was opened to define these sources

gps_format_freeze.rule: after the first two documentation/header lines, every remaining physical line must split into exactly 9 tab-separated fields and satisfy the frozen W/Waypoint markers; node name, latitude and longitude are taken at the frozen indices without aliasing or row deletion

candidate_response_source.published_role: Ecological Archives E092-148-S1: estimated population sizes for each glade for every year of occupation on Stegall, Mule and Thorny Mountains
candidate_response_source.reason: this glade-by-year supplement is closer to the frozen node-time endpoint than individual capture records; it must be independently machine-readable and physically separate from GPS geometry before any payload access
